correctness.rationale: For each opposite edge pair, equality of squared lengths forces its common displacement difference perpendicular to the baseline edge. Equilateralness yields one magnitude t and signs, with cyclic closure exactly Q(zeta)=0. Phi_{2m}=x^m+1 gives complete dyadic obstruction; an odd-divisor block construction gives Q(zeta)=0 otherwise. Exact Pythagorean side formula, positive turning-determinant margin, and the strict nonopposite distance gap cos(pi/n)<1 establish diameter-one convex small configurations for small t>0. The standalone checker passed 24 symbolic and finite-geometric cases plus five dyadic polynomial checks. Computations are corroboration, not an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The active antipodal diameters of a regular even polygon define a natural moduli restriction in the small-polygon perimeter problem. The theorem provides an exact all-even-n classification in that class, a sharp cyclotomic arithmetic obstruction and a constructive local gain with all those active vector constraints preserved to every order. These conclusions are stronger and geometrically different from the already established fact that odd-factor n admits an unrelated global nonregular maximizer.
